title: The Consignment Watch
tagline: A $4,800 pocket watch vanishes from a locked safe. The apprentice took the blame.
hook: A gold pocket watch goes missing overnight from a small watchmaker's shop. The alarm log shows the apprentice let himself in at 22:14, and the first officer never looked further. The owner of the watch wants a second opinion. This is your first file, and a guide will walk you through the desk.
note: New here? Start with this one. A guide shows you every tool.
advice: Every one of these was suggested by something in the file. Before you spend, ask what in the file made you want it.

persons.label: Eliminations
persons.hint: A person is eliminated only when a document puts them beyond the theft.

rules: The documents don't lie. People might. If a statement and a log disagree, the log is right.
The whole file is yours. The tension is in what you spend, not what you hide.
You have a fixed number of Authorities and they do not come back. Not every one returns something useful.
Write your working on the Resolution Sheet as you establish it, with document references. Anything not written before the final accusation scores nothing.
You get two wrong accusations. Each costs 10 points and opens a Reconsider envelope naming the gap in your theory. The third accusation is final.
When you are done, break the seal on Envelope S-1 and read it in order.

hints.q: Could Theo have taken it at night?
steps: The watch was kept in a safe. Does the safe keep a record?
D-1 section 2 lists every time the safe opened. Look at Friday night.
The safe did not open between 17:57 and 08:34, and D-1 section 3 shows Theo has no safe code.

hints.q: When did the watch really go?
steps: Compare what Priya says about the safe (C-1) with the safe log (D-1 section 2).
The safe opened at 16:38 and did not close until 17:57. Who was in the shop at the end of that?
E-1.1: from 17:30 one person was in the shop. The watch went before the safe closed.
Look for something in the file that nobody has checked.
D-1 section 5: a camera over the counter that the first officer never reviewed.
Spend Authority 03. Authority 04 gives the motive; 06 clears Mrs Hollis.

tutorial.intro: I will show you each tool as you need it. Skip any step, shrink me with the - button, or send me away with the X.
tutorial.handover: That is every tool on the desk. The rest of the case is yours: fill in the sheet, clear who you can, and accuse when you are sure.

tasks.text: Open A-1, the crime report. It tells you what the first officer decided, and why.
Select a time in any document, like 22:14 in A-1, and press Highlight. Highlighted times build a timeline in your notebook.
Now the logs. Open D-1, the shop systems extract. Logs don't lie; people might.
Could the watch have gone at night? Open the Resolution Sheet, answer step 2 and cite the document that proves it, like D-1.
Spend one Authority: pick an envelope on the right. D-1 section 5 says what nobody checked.

full.text: Read Priya Desai's statement, C-1. What does she say she did with the safe after the viewing?
Compare her words with the safe log in D-1 section 2, and the rota in E-1.1. Write step 3 on the sheet: who was alone with the open safe? Cite D-1 and E-1.
Spend Authority 03, the counter camera nobody reviewed.
Write step 4: whose account fails? Cite C-1, D-1 and SLIP 03.
Fill in step 1: when was the watch last seen? Priya's own statement, C-1, tells you.
Clear Theo. Click his photo under Persons of interest and mark him Eliminated. The safe log and staff codes (D-1) put him beyond it.
Clear Mrs Hollis too: she left at 17:30 (E-1.1) and the tray went into the safe empty (SLIP 03).
On the Resolution Sheet, add the evidence for both eliminations, so they score.
You have it. Press Accuse and name who took the watch.
